cards.label: Hackney — the back of a shop that sells phone cases
cards.text: Nadia Beckford is about seventy and is moving a crate that you would need help with. She does not accept help.

cards.speaker: Nadia
cards.text: "Des sent you. He's told you I'm short." She doesn't look up. "He's right. I'm short."

cards.speaker: Nadia
cards.text: "Standing order. Emotion calc, every fortnight, same bloke, same amount, been running four years. It pays for a lot of things that need paying for."

cards.speaker: Nadia
cards.text: "Whitechapel's full of it and everyone round here has a bit and nobody has thirty units at once. So I spend three days on the phone every fortnight like it's 1974."

choices.label: I can get you thirty
choices.result_text: "Course you can." She goes back to the crate. "Bring it when you've got it. Bring it in bits, I don't care."

choices.label: What's in it for me?
choices.result_text: "Market rate, same as anyone." A pause. "You were expecting me to be offended. I'm not. Ask people what things cost, it saves everybody a fortnight."

cards.speaker: Nadia
cards.text: "And before you ask — no, I don't know who's holding what. Nobody does. If I knew who had what I'd have had this done Tuesday."
Thirty units of emotion calc, no deadline, no paperwork, and a woman who has been doing this since before you were born treating it as entirely routine.
